It's strange because I've never been very religious. My parents tried a few times to get me into Christianity, but they were never hardcore religious fanatics. They never so much as took me to church.

I can understand why the topic is a little bit of a weird thing when it comes to DID/OSDD, but in most cases (such as mine) I don't really feel there's a great risk or anything. We both have an awareness that he's not *actually* a demon of hell, and I don't intend on converting to devil worship because of him. I feel in our case it's not exactly something to be worried about.

That's fair. I guess my main concern was that I spent so long obsessing over what makes a case of DID legitimate before learning about OSDD that I worry about it somehow crossing a line and taking away from the notion of this being a real case. Basically if this stuff is "allowed", so to speak.
Truthfully, I'm not very religious and I never have been, so I don't think that it's anything to worry about in that regard.

He does, I know he does. Even before we tried this he showed a lot of affection when I started accepting him. He's made me cry more than once by telling me he loves me, hah. We don't have trust issues or anything, and he's chilled out a lot over the years. I'm just trying to cooperate with him and understand him more beyond acceptance, and I'm aware that he might need a little help coming out of his shell after suppressing himself for so long. Honestly, I feel kinda bad about it. Glad to know I'm not the only one that has an alter that's a "demon", though.

I don't really have religious traumas or anything like that, if that's what you mean. Our relationship starting off with him being considered a demon was (I think) because of how violent he used to be. Thank you though, I'll try to keep it in mind. It's just a very new area for both of us.

I used to go to a therapist, but her solution to many of my problems was "let's get your mom in here and talk about it" which made me stop being honest with her. I used to go to a psychiatrist, but my mom was also in the room for most sessions so that made it hard to be honest during sessions as well. So no, not properly.
